paragraphs.text: I'm one of the biggest fish on earth!
Great white sharks live in the ocean.
We like to swim in cool water.
But we don't usually attack people.
We also eat sea lions, dolphins, and turtles.
So you have to hunt for food?
We can smell our prey from far away.
We have about three hundred of them.
Great white sharks are very fast!
Our tails are long and powerful.
They help us shoot through the water.
Gorillas are the biggest kind of apes.
We live in the mountains of Africa.
We hoot and roar when we're mad.
We growl softly when we're happy.
We mostly eat plants and tree bark.
We really like plants' stems, roots, and leaves.
They steal our land and hunt us.
But some people try to protect us.
The big silverback is our boss.
He tells us what to do.
I hear the silverback calling me now.
We're the biggest reptiles on earth.
Nile crocodiles live mostly in Africa.
We like warm swamps, rivers, and marshes.
We have more than sixty teeth.
But we can't chew with them.
We eat fish, turtles, and crabs.
Our strong jaws open very wide.
So we can eat zebras and hippos too.
Yes! Nile crocodiles are very dangerous.
But Nile crocodiles are very caring parents.
Most reptiles don't stay with their eggs.
We use our powerful tails to move.
Our eyes and ears stay above the water.
That helps us see and hear.
I'm ready for a swim now.
Cheetahs are a type of large cat.
We're the fastest land animal on earth!
We live in open grasslands called savannas.
You have lots of cool spots.
Cheetahs are covered with black dots.
They help us hide in the grass.
Cheetahs mostly eat small animals like hares.
But we also eat big animals like antelopes!
How do cheetahs run so fast?
We're also thin, with small heads.
Cheetahs probably always catch their prey.
Cheetahs can only run for about a minute.
We spot our prey and sneak closer . . .
Once we're close enough, we run—fast!
That's a type of brown bear.
I live in Alaska like many grizzly bears.
We live in forests, meadows, and tundra.
Yes, and we can run fast too.
But a mother grizzly bear is very dangerous.
She'll attack anyone who goes near her cubs.
We eat berries, leaves, roots, and nuts.
Sometimes we eat small animals or even moose.
Grizzly bears go fishing too, right?
We eat lots of salmon in the fall.
That's when we get really fat.
Why do you eat so much?
We go into a deep sleep during winter.
We will not eat again until spring.
My winter den is ready now.
Wolves are a kind of wild dog.
We're bigger than most pet dogs.
I live in the United States.
Wolves live in other parts of the world too.
We live in forests and tundra, and on prairies.
Lots of people think we're dangerous.
But we almost never hurt people.
Sometimes we eat small animals like hares.
We also hunt bison and moose.
Whoa! Bison and moose are big animals!
Yes, but wolves live in packs.
We all work together to hunt big prey.
How do wolves learn to hunt?
They pretend to fight each other.
He howls to keep our pack together.
I've got to join my pack now.
Great horned owls live in many places.
We like forests, tundra, and even cities.
We often make nests in tree holes.
We can fly without making a sound.
Our eyes help us see in the dark.
We use our sharp claws to kill prey.
Our claws help us carry food too.
We eat mice, raccoons, and sometimes skunks.
Then we spit up the bones and fur.
Are those horns on your head?
No, they are just tall feathers.
But these feathers look like horns!
They caw loudly and chase us.
We live near the Arctic Circle.
Blubber is a type of fat.
It keeps us nice and warm.
We use them to poke holes in ice.
Our tusks also protect us from enemies.
But we can swim for a long time.
Walruses mostly eat clams from the ocean floor.
We use our whiskers to find the clams.
Do you live with other walruses?
Yes, walruses live in big groups.
We like to lie on the beach together.
Mollusks have soft bodies and no bones.
We like to crawl along the ocean floor.
You have a lot of arms!
But we can grow a new one.
We can even taste with them!
We really like clams and crabs.
Seals and big fish often eat us.
We can change color and shape.
We use the water to move backward.
Then we shoot the water out and—zoom!
We're the biggest rays on earth.
We have flat bodies and long tails.
Manta rays live in the ocean.
We like to swim in warm water.
We eat very tiny fish and plants.
We swim with our mouths open to catch plankton.
Sharks and whales like to eat us.
Sometimes we get stuck in people's fishing nets.
But manta rays don't have stingers.
We are usually calm and gentle around people.
Our fins are like huge wings.
We flap them to move through the water.
We can even dive and do loops.
I see some plankton. Watch this!
Those are birds that stay near shallow water.
Great blue herons live in North America.
We like rivers, ponds, marshes, and fields.
We eat insects, mice, and even snakes.
But we like fish best of all.
We stand in the water without moving.
We wait for fish to swim by.
Then we use our sharp bills as spears.
We lay about five eggs at a time.
We keep them in nests in high trees.
But raccoons and eagles sometimes eat young herons.
We can spread them very wide.
I look like a dinosaur in the sky!
A lot of raccoons live in North America.
We live in forests, marshes, and cities.
We usually make dens high in trees.
We also have rings on our tails.
We love fish, berries, mice, and frogs.
Is it hard to find food in cities?
We find great food in garbage cans.
Our front paws are like your hands.
We have five fingers on each paw.
We can grab things and even open doors.
Do you live with other raccoons?
Yes, raccoons live in small groups.
We look for food at night.
Oh! I smell food in that garbage can.
Tigers are the largest cats on earth.
We make our homes in forests.
We're the only big cats that like water.
Our stripes help us hide in the forest.
Then our prey can't see us!
We hunt big animals like elk and bears.
We can see very well in the dark.
We have sharp teeth and claws.
But we usually stay away from people.
Do you live with other tigers?
We stay away from each other.
Rattlesnakes live in North and South America.
We live in prairies, forests, and deserts.
We shake our rattles to warn enemies.
We love rabbits, mice, and prairie dogs!
Our tongues are shaped like forks.
We can sense heat from prey too.
We use our fangs to bite.
Then we swallow the animal whole!
Yes, we shed our skin as we grow.
We rub against rocks to loosen it.
Then we crawl right out of our skin!
Peregrine falcons are the fastest animals on earth.
Peregrine falcons live all over the world.
We like being close to the sea.
We eat other birds like ducks or pigeons.
We watch from a high place.
We wait for other birds to fly by.
Is it hard to see from up high?
We can spot small animals from far away.
Is that when you fly fast?
Yes! We dive down toward our prey.
Eagles and owls sometimes try to eat us.
But we don't have many enemies.
Oh! I see a flock of pigeons!
Giraffes are the tallest land mammals on earth.
Yes, we can run really fast.
And we look for food all day long.
Our long legs help us roam the grasslands.
We look for food in very tall trees.
We can reach food with our long necks.
Our favorite leaves have lots of water.
So we don't need to drink often.
Well, all giraffes have coats with spots.
But our coats have different patterns.
That makes every giraffe look different.
We take just a short nap each day.
I see a tasty leaf. Bye.
Black widow spiders live all over the world.
We often hide under rocks or in basements.
Our markings look like an hourglass.
We like flies, beetles, and grasshoppers.
Then we wait for bugs to come by.
The bugs get caught in our webs.
How do you make a web?
The silk is very strong and sticky.
Our bites can make people very sick.
Oh! I trapped a grasshopper in my web!
We're the biggest kind of bat.
Most flying foxes live in Asia and Australia.
But we like rain forests and swamps.
Flying foxes live in huge groups.
Some groups have a million flying foxes!
Yes, our wings are very strong.
We can carry our babies while flying.
We hang upside down from branches.
Flying foxes mostly eat nectar from flowers.
Is it hard to find food?
We can also smell things from far away.
We're the biggest land mammals on earth.
We live in grasslands and rain forests.
Some African elephants live in deserts.
We spray our backs with water.
Then we throw dust on the water.
We use our trunks for that.
We breathe and drink with our trunks.
We can grab food with them too.
We like leaves, bark, roots, fruit, and grass.
We're big. So we eat a lot!
We use them to dig for roots.
But some people hunt us for our tusks.
Eastern box turtles live in the United States.
We like forests, meadows, and marshes.
We usually live near ponds and streams.
We go in the water to cool off.
Older Eastern box turtles mostly eat plants.
But younger ones like fish, snails, and bugs.
We can live for a long time.
Some of us live over a hundred years!
Yes, we dig holes with our back legs.
Then we lay eggs in the hole.
Babies crawl out three months later.
I'm going to hide in my shell.
Ladybugs live all over the world.
We like forests, rivers, and even houses.
Some people call us "ladybirds" or "lady beetles."
We like bugs that eat plants.
Ladybugs are usually red, yellow, or orange.
But most have black spots like mine.
Why do you have those spots?
Our spots and bright colors keep enemies away.
They warn animals that we taste bad!
So do frogs, spiders, and dragonflies.
Yes. We sleep under rocks or inside old logs.
Sometimes we go into houses to get warm.
Porcupines live all over the world.
We live in snowbanks and the desert too.
We bite it with our big teeth.
We also like grass and fruit.
You have needles on your fur!
They lie flat unless an enemy comes near.
What do the quills do then?
They can stick into enemies' skin.
They are very hard to get out.
But others stay on the ground.
Hey, it's a giant pink bird!
Those are birds that stay near shallow water.
We live all over the world.
We like lakes, ponds, and oceans.
Flamingos live together in big groups.
Wow! You can stand on one leg!
Yes, we stand on one leg to rest.
And we stand on two legs to eat.
We like snails, plants, and fish.
We also eat lots of shrimp.
Their pink color makes our feathers turn pink!
Our long neck helps us to fish.
And our bill is like a shovel.
We use it to scoop up food.
We can also run on the water.
Gastropods have soft bodies and no bones.
Garden snails live in gardens and forests.
Do snails hide during the day?
We often hide under rocks or old logs.
Then we come out at night.
Snails have two sets of tentacles.
Our eyes are on the top tentacles.
We smell with our bottom tentacles.
Garden snails move very, very slowly.
We leave slime trails wherever we go.
Garden snails eat plants and old wood.
Our tongues have thousands of tiny teeth!
I'm going to find something to eat!
Beavers live in North America and Europe.
We like to be in fresh water.
Can beavers really cut down trees?
Yes. We use our sharp teeth for that.
What do you do with the trees?
We also use the branches to build things.
Our dams stop streams and make ponds.
We build our homes in those ponds.
What are your homes made of?
They are made of sticks and mud.
We use the canals to carry our branches.
We also slap the water with them.
That warns other beavers that enemies are near.
Giant pandas are a type of bear.
We're one of the rarest mammals on earth.
Giant pandas mostly eat bamboo shoots and leaves.
We eat a lot and we eat fast.
We eat for 12 hours a day!
Yes, giant pandas are great climbers.
We can also swim very well.
Do giant pandas hibernate in winter?
We just find a warmer place for winter.
Giant pandas sleep in many different places.
Sometimes we nap in hollow logs.
I'm going to eat more bamboo.
Female marsupials carry their babies in pouches.
We like open grasslands and deserts.
Joeys sometimes come out to explore.
After ten months they leave the pouch forever.
Red kangaroos eat grass and leaves.
We can last for several days without water.
Male kangaroos often fight with their front paws.
They also kick with their back legs.
Wild dogs called dingoes hunt us.
We stomp our feet when danger is near.
Our feet are very strong too.
Red kangaroos can jump up to 12 meters!
Many people just call us hippos.
We stay near swamps, lakes, and rivers.
Yes. Hippos spend almost all day in the water.
We even sleep in shallow water.
So we often just walk through the water.
We usually wait until the hot sun sets.
Then we leave the water to find food.
Our jaws can open very wide.
Our bottom teeth are long—and sharp!
Oh! Do you have many enemies?
We're too big to have many enemies.
African lions live in Africa, right?
We live near grasslands and woodlands.
But lions live in groups called prides.
A pride usually has about 15 lions.
The manes make us look bigger.
That helps us to protect our pride.
Male lions roar more than females.
We roar to call our prides.
We also scare other animals away.
We mostly eat wildebeests, zebras, and antelopes.
Sometimes we eat small rodents too.
No. Female lions hunt for the whole pride.
I like your black and white stripes!
But every zebra’s stripes look different.
That means we eat a lot of grass.
We move often to find water and food.
You have a lot of teeth!
Our teeth help us bite and chew grass.
No. We stay with our families.
Our families travel in big herds.
Some herds have thousands of zebras!
Why do zebras bite each other?
Zebras don't really bite each other.
We just use our teeth for grooming.
We keep other zebras' coats clean.
It’s time to look for water again.
Female marsupials carry their babies in pouches.
We like to be in trees.
We use our feet to grab branches.
Yes. Each koala has its own trees.
We mark our trees with scratches.
Male koalas mark their trees with their scent.
Koalas sleep up in the trees.
We sleep for most of the day!
Koalas eat leaves from one kind of tree.
We have pouches in our cheeks.
We store extra leaves in them.
We're usually safe in our trees.
But wild dogs and owls sometimes eat koalas.
I'm tired from eating so many leaves!
Skunks live in North and South America.
A lot of skunks have stripes.
All skunks are black and white.
Skunks eat bugs and small animals.
We also like plants and fruit.
Skunks look for food at night.
Skunks sleep in hollow logs or holes.
Sometimes we sleep in other animals' homes.
But most animals stay away from us.
Why do they stay away from you?
We shoot enemies with the spray.
Red-eyed tree frogs live in North and South America.
We live in trees near water.
We like crickets, moths, and flies.
We catch prey with our long, sticky tongues.
We sleep on the bottoms of leaves.
We can stick to the leaves!
Birds and snakes try to eat us.
But our colors help protect us.
Our green bodies blend in with leaves.
What if an enemy sees you?
Our red eyes can surprise enemies.
Our orange legs also surprise enemies.
Oh no! I see a snake!
Land hermit crabs live in tropical areas.
Land hermit crabs eat almost anything.
We like leaves, wood, and grass.
I grab food with my small claw.
I can climb with my big claw.
Why do you have that shell?
A part of our body is soft.
Where do you get your shells?
We find our shells on the beach.
Land hermit crabs grow a lot.
So sometimes we need to find bigger shells!
Land hermit crabs live in groups.
We help each other find food and shells.
I see a bigger shell now!
We are mammals with humps on our backs.
We live in the rocky desert.
Is it hard to live in the desert?
Yes. It gets very hot and very cold.
The wind blows sand and ice at us.
We can close our nose holes.
Then sand and ice can't blow into them.
And our long eyelashes protect our eyes.
Why do you have those humps?
Food and water are hard to find here.
Fat helps us go without food or water.
We're the biggest penguins in the world.
We live on the cold ice.
Emperor penguins can dive very deep.
The mother penguin lays one egg.
Then the father takes care of the egg.
How does the father do that?
He holds the egg on his feet.
Then he doesn't eat or go anywhere.
After two months the egg finally hatches.
We huddle together in the cold.
We take turns standing in the warmest spots.
I'm ready to dive again. Good-bye!
Parrots are a type of bird.
Parrots live all over the world.
Most parrots like warm places like rain forests.
But some live in snowy places.
Parrots mostly eat nuts and seeds.
We use them to crack open nuts and seeds.
Do all parrots look the same?
No. There are many different kinds of parrots.
But we all have curved beaks.
And we all have four toes!
Yep. Parrots are very smart birds.
Some parrots can learn words from people.
We can imitate other sounds too.
Parrots live in groups called flocks.
We like to talk to each other.
They often take us for pets.
But white rhinos are actually gray.
Most white rhinos live in South Africa.
So we can eat a lot at once!
Why do you roll in mud?
Mud protects us from the hot sun.
Oh! Do you have many enemies?
White rhinos fight each other sometimes.
But people are our main enemy.
They hunt us for our horns.
Sometimes white rhinos run very fast.
But we're too big to run for long.
I'm going to rest in the shade now.
Sea otters are a type of weasel.
Sea otters live in the Pacific Ocean.
We live in North America and Asia.
Do you ever go on land?
Sea otters go on land to rest sometimes.
But we mostly stay in the water.
We even sleep in the water.
Sometimes we sleep wrapped in kelp.
The kelp keeps us from drifting away.
Sea otters eat fish and octopuses.
We also like crabs and clams.
We use rocks to break them open.
Our fur keeps us warm and dry.
Killer whales and sharks sometimes eat us.
Our webbed feet help us swim away fast.
I need to clean my fur now.
Cottontails are mammals with long ears.
Cottontails live in North and South America.
We like open fields and meadows.
Cottontails mostly eat grasses and herbs.
We love vegetables like lettuce and peas!
We eat after the sun goes down.
That keeps us safe from enemies.
Yes, cottontails have a lot of enemies!
Owls, hawks, and foxes often hunt us.
But we can run away very fast!
Cottontails have brown or gray fur.
But we all have the same kind of tail.
It looks like a white cotton ball!
Yes. We make shallow nests underground.
Our babies are very tiny when they're born.
I'm going back into the nest now.
You live in the sea, right?
Manatees live in oceans and rivers.
So we move to stay warm.
Sometimes we eat tiny fish by mistake.
Yes. Some people call us sea cows.
We both have thick skin and toenails.
Do you ever go on land?
No. Manatees stay in the water.
But we come up often for air.
We use our strong tails to move.
They also pollute our oceans and rivers.
Raptors are birds that hunt for food.
We like open places like fields.
Yes. We are a big help to nature.
We clean up fields and roads.
And we never attack living animals.
We fly and sleep together too.
We can even eat big animals.
We look for holes in rocks or logs.
We like old buildings and caves too.
We live in Africa and Arabia.
We like fruit, insects, and bark.
Sometimes we eat birds or even sheep.
We usually stay on the ground.
But we climb trees to watch for enemies.
You live in a big group!
We talk to each other by making sounds.
We remove dirt and bugs from each other.
Big cats like cheetahs and lions hunt us.
We stay near a plant called milkweed.
We live in North America in spring and summer.
In the fall we fly away.
Monarch butterflies usually fly to Mexico.
Yes. We fly thousands of kilometers.
I've never made the trip before.
But I'll know where to go.
Monarch butterflies sip nectar from flowers.
Butterflies lay eggs on milkweed leaves.
Baby caterpillars hatch from the eggs.
The caterpillars begin eating and growing.
How do the caterpillars become butterflies?
Their skin turns into a hard case.
Ten days later butterflies fly out!
Well, it's time to fly away.
Have a safe trip, Monarch Butterfly!
We live all over the world.
We like bark and flowers too.
Our long back legs help us jump.
We can jump very high and very far.
Most grasshoppers have wings and can fly.
Our legs help us spring into the air.
Many animals like to eat us.
But our colors help us hide.
We can hop away fast too!
But sometimes we gather in big groups.
I'm going to jump over there.
We live around the Arctic Ocean.
We like the ice along the coast.
Our thick fur keeps us warm.
We also have a layer of fat.
We use our big paws for that.
We need fat in the cold weather.
We wait next to holes in the ice.
I see a hole in the ice.
I'm the biggest bird in the world.
We like the savanna and the desert.
We can run very fast though.
We can kick enemies with them.
We get water from them too.
Sometimes we eat bugs or lizards.
Do you live in a herd?
One male ostrich is in charge.
Females put all their eggs together.
Do ostriches stick their heads in the ground?
We just put our heads near the ground.
That helps us hide from enemies.
We live all over the world.
No. We come up often for air.
We also like squid and crabs.
No. Bottlenose dolphins live in big groups.
Wow! You can jump out of the water!
We can get caught in fishing nets too.
Brown pelicans live in North America.
Sometimes we make nests in trees.
No. Brown pelicans live in groups.
We like to fly over the water together.
Sometimes we eat shrimp or crabs.
We hunt from up in the air.
We can catch lots of fish with them.
Most sea lions live near the Pacific Ocean.
We can walk with our strong flippers.
You have a lot of friends!
Sea lions live in big groups.
We lie in the sun together.
We also like squid and shellfish.
Great white sharks hunt us too.

We live in the United States.
We swim in rivers, lakes, and swamps.
We like frogs, fish, snails, and mammals.
I can even crack a turtle's hard shell!
We grab prey with our sharp teeth.
We can roar like lions too.
No. But we sleep in holes sometimes.
We find a muddy spot in water.
Then we dig holes to keep warm.
My tail moves me through the water.
We live near fields and meadows.
We usually stay close to forests.
We like grasses, plants, and fruit.
Sometimes we eat tree bark or bugs too.
We eat a lot in summer and fall.
But we don't eat during winter.
Yes. We climb trees and bushes.
We use our claws to dig deep holes.
Our holes have rooms and tunnels.
Red foxes live all over the world.
But we also live in cities and deserts.
Yes. We eat other small animals too.
Our big ears help us hear prey.
They hunt us and build near our dens.
Yes. We use dens for sleeping.

We use our tails to cover our bodies.
This keeps us warm at nap time.
Moose are the biggest kind of deer.
Moose live in cold parts of the world.
We stay near lakes, ponds, or streams.
Our hooves help us walk in snow.
We eat twigs, bark, leaves, and pinecones.
We also eat plants that grow in water.

We use antlers to find mates and fight.
Bears, wolves, and cougars hunt us.

We travel very far every year.
We live in cold water in the summer.
We swim to warm water for the winter.
We eat small sea creatures and fish.
Humpback whales make lots of sounds.

Our tails help us jump out of the water.

We live in warm places like Central America.

Sometimes we break off our tails.
Yes! We use our claws to climb.
We spend lots of time in trees.
We eat leaves, fruit, and flowers.

Sometimes we hide from enemies in the water.
We can stay underwater for a long time.

We swim near rocks and reefs.
Clown fish eat lots of plants.
Some fish are afraid of them.

No. Clown fish have different colors.

We scratch the ground to find food.
Right! Males are bigger than females.

Yes! Male turkeys make a loud gobble sound.

Yes. We eat lots and lots of ants.

We like to be near fresh water.
Oh. Do you like warm weather?
The sun warms up our wings.

Yes! Dragonflies catch prey in the air.

No! We are the slowest fish.

American bison live in North America.
Yes, but we can run fast.

American bison eat lots and lots of grass.
We also like leaves and weeds.

Sometimes we join a big herd.

Geckos live all over the world.
We like rain forests and deserts.
But some geckos live in cold places.

But geckos also click and chirp.

We live in Africa and Asia.
